title: Fabrication of a Multiplexed Artificial Cellular MicroEnvironment Array
protocol: Create three-dimensional images of masks for nanofiber arrays and molds for microfluidic structures using 3D-computer graphics software packages.
Print masks and a mold based on these designs using a 3D printer.
Dilute 13% PMGI liquid with tetrahydrofuran by 9% (w/v).
Dissolve 0.08 g of PS in THF:dimethylformamide (1:1 volume ratio) to prepare an 8% (w/v) solution.
Dissolve 0.1 g of GT in water:acetic acid:ethyl acetate (1:1.6:2.1 volume ratio) to prepare a 10% (w/v) solution.
Deposit a thin platinum layer with a 5-nm thickness on a polystyrene (PS) baseplate using a magnetron sputtering machine.
Load each polymer solution into a 5-mL syringe equipped with a 23-G stainless-steel blunt needle.
Anchor the syringe with the needle on a syringe pump at a distance of 12 cm from the collector of the electrospinning device.
Connect the syringe needle to a high-voltage power supply and set it to apply 11 kV.
Set the pumping rate of the syringe pump to 0.2 mL/h.
Maintain temperature and humidity at 30 °C and < 30% (v/v).
Place and anchor the mask on the baseplate prepared in step 1.2.2.
Fabricate nanofibers on the baseplate through the holes of the mask by changing the electrospinning time (e.g., 20, 60, 90, and 180 s).
Remove the mask from the baseplate.
Spray ethanol on the electrospun GT nanofibers before removing the mask to avoid peeling off GT nanofibers together with the mask.
Repeat steps involving fabricating nanofiber arrays until completion.
Place the fabricated nanofiber array in a desiccator at 25 °C for 16 h to evaporate remaining solvent.
Crosslink GT nanofibers with 0.2 M EDC and 0.2 M NHS in ethanol at 25 °C for 4 hours.
Rinse GT nanofibers twice with 99.5% (v/v) ethanol.
Vacuum-dry the rinsed nanofibers at 25 °C for 16 h.
Mix 2 g of PDMS curing agent and 20 g of PDMS base (1:10 weight ratio; Pre-PDMS).
Pour the pre-PDMS mixture onto the mold fabricated in step 1.2.
De-gas the pre-PDMS mixture in a desiccator for 30 min.
Cure the pre-PDMS mixture in an oven at 65 °C for 16 h.
Peel off the PDMS structure cured at step 1.3.4 from the mold.
Clean the PDMS structure with 70% (v/v) ethanol.
Treat atmospheric corona discharge on the bottom side of the PDMS structure.
Assemble the PDMS structure with the nanofiber array quickly.
Oven-bake the assembled PDMS structure at 65°C for 2 days.
Sterilize a MACME array with 99.5% ethanol by loading into the chambers for 10 min.
Remove the ethanol from the MACME array after sterilization.
Repeat the sterilization step 3 times.
Introduce 12 µL of MG into control culture chambers.
Incubate the chambers at 37 °C for 1 h to coat them on the chamber surfaces.
Introduce 10 µg/mL vitronectin (VN) into control culture chambers.
Incubate the chambers at 37 °C for 1 h to coat them on the chamber surfaces.
Introduce 0.1% (w/v) GT into control culture chambers.
Incubate the chambers at 37 °C for 1 h to coat them on the chamber surfaces.
Introduce pre-warmed hPSC medium into all chambers of MACME array.
Incubate the chambers for 30 min at 37 °C.
Wash H9 hESC cultured on a 35-mm dish with DPBS.
Add 0.5 mL of a recombinant trypsin-like protease to the dish and incubate at 37 °C for 1 min.
Carefully aspirate only the supernatants mixed with protease from the dish.
Immediately add hPSC medium to the dish, gently dispense the medium against the dish surface repeatedly to dissociate cells.
Transfer the detached cells to a 15-mL conical tube.
Centrifuge at 200 x g for 3 min.
Aspirate the supernatant and suspend cells in pre-warmed hPSC medium.
Introduce 12 µL of the cell suspension (1.2 × 10^6 cells/mL) into each microfluidic chamber.
Introduce cells to one chamber from another using a micropipette.
Ensure pipetting is done gently.
Remove excess medium from the chambers using a cotton-tipped stick after loading.
Change hPSC medium every 12 hours and culture for 4 days.
Incubate H9 hESCs in MACME arrays in hPSC medium supplemented with 10 μM EdU alkyne at 37 °C for 30 minutes.
Wash cells with annexin-binding buffer.
Stain cells with an orange-fluorescent dye-Annexin V conjugate at 20°C for 15 min.
Fix cells in PBS with 4% (v/v) paraformaldehyde at 20°C for 15 min.
Rinse cells with PBS twice.
Permeabilize cells using PBS with 0.3% (v/v) Triton X-100 at 20°C for 16 h.
Incubate cells in Tris-based reaction buffer with a red-fluorescent dye azide at 20°C for 30 min.

Incubate cells in blocking buffer (PBS with 5% (v/v) normal goat serum, 5% (v/v) normal donkey serum, 3% (w/v) bovine serum albumin, 0.1% (v/v) Tween-20, and 0.1% (w/v) N-dodecyl-β-D-maltoside) at 4°C for 16 h.
Incubate in PBS with 0.5% (v/v) Triton X-100 solution and human OCT3/4 antibody (mouse IgG) at 4°C for 16 h.
Incubate in blocking buffer with green-fluorescent dye-labeled donkey anti-mouse IgG (H+L) at 37°C for 60 min.
Incubate in PBS with DAPI at 20°C for 30 min.
Replace PBS-DAPI with PBS.
Preserve the MACME array at 4°C until image acquisition.
Peel off the PDMS microfluidic structure from the MACME array.
Remove residual PBS from the MACME array.
Apply 90% (v/v) glycerol in PBS to the cells.
Place coverslips over the stained cells.
Set the plate upside down on the stage of an inverted fluorescence microscope.
Acquire 12-bit color images using all motorized components controlled by a microscope imaging software.
Convert color images to grayscale.
Calculate a single threshold value for each DAPI image with the Otsu method.
Classify pixels above the threshold as foreground and below as background in DAPI images.
Measure the fluorescent intensities of OCT4 on each image.
Measure the fluorescent intensities of EdU on each image.
Identify the region stained with Annexin V using the propagation method.
Quantify the fluorescent intensity of Annexin V.
Normalize input fluorescent intensities of each phenotypic marker by centering and scaling these variables.
Perform self-organizing map (SOM) analysis using a software environment for statistical computing and graphics.
Create 25 SOM nodes with distinctive four "codebook vectors" corresponding to the fluorescent intensities of DAPI, EdU, Annexin V, and OCT4.
Assign individual cells in each microenvironment to a "winning" node based on similarity.
Update codebook vectors of winning nodes using a weighted average where the weight is the learning rate (0.05 as default).
Omit data from chambers containing less than 1,000 cells.
Perform unsupervised hierarchical clustering with SOM-node values using the average-linkage method based on Pearson correlation by a clustering software.
Render the clustering data into dendrogram and heatmap views.
